_comment: Every substantive data layer points here by source_id. licence_status is one of: verified | conditional | unresolved | internal | provisional. in_use=false entries are registered for traceability only: nothing in the dataset is derived from them. No entry claims commercial clearance, because research has not established it for any source.

sources.name: Tanzil Quran text (Uthmani)
sources.version: 1.1 (release of 12 Feb 2021; file header reads 'Uthmani, Version 1.1', copyright 2007-2026)
sources.licence: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 (Tanzil Project). Terms read on https://tanzil.net/docs/Text_License : verbatim copies only, changing the text is not allowed; the source (Tanzil Project) must be clearly indicated with a link to tanzil.net; the copyright block must be kept in verbatim copies and reproduced in derived files.
sources.allowed_use: Display and search of the Qur'anic text unmodified, with attribution + link (shown in the app footer and Source panel); the copyright block is retained in data/raw/tanzil/quran-uthmani.txt. Normalised forms are stored separately and never displayed.
sources.notes: Downloaded from tanzil.net/pub/download/index.php on 2026-10-06 with parameters quranType=uthmani, outType=txt-2, and every optional symbol switched off (no pause marks, no sajdah signs, no rub-el-hizb signs, no tatweel), after the terms checkbox was ticked on QURRA's behalf with the owner's approval. File SHA-256: bf4f57b968d03f4131c070b1e285da9be0e0a108a21c910e872801ca273312c8 (6,236 ayah lines). The official file prefixes the basmala onto ayah 1 of every surah except 1 and 9 (two spellings: 110 lines use 'بِسْمِ', and 95:1 and 97:1 use 'بِّسْمِ' with an extra shadda in the official file); the raw file keeps it verbatim and data/qurra/ayahs.json separates it as source_prefix. 'Verified' here means the text and its licence terms come from the official source and the Stage 2 pilot was diffed against it (see STAGE_3_REPORT.md); it does not assert any wider commercial clearance beyond the CC BY 3.0 terms. Pause marks are omitted by choice (a Tanzil-supported option) to keep word tokens clean; they can be re-added from a new official download.

gate.commercial_use: permitted (CC BY 3.0 has no non-commercial clause)
gate.static_bundling: yes: 'can be used in any website or application' with the source indicated and a link
gate.derivatives: text must not be changed; normalised search forms are stored separately and never displayed
gate.attribution: required: Tanzil Project + link to tanzil.net + the copyright block in derived files
gate.third_party_material: none stated
gate.reason: Official source, terms read at tanzil.net; notice carried in every derived file.

sources.name: Marmaduke Pickthall, The Meaning of the Glorious Koran (1930), English translation
sources.version: 1930 text, as transcribed in gutenberg.org e-text #16955 (release 27 Oct 2005, updated 12 Dec 2020)
sources.licence: Public domain: the translator died in 1936 and the work was first published in 1930. The transcription's catalogue record states 'Public domain in the USA'.
sources.allowed_use: Display of the translation text verbatim; searchable.
sources.notes: Only the Pickthall column was taken (the e-text also holds two other translations, which were NOT taken: their copyright status is not as clear). The raw download is kept outside git in staging/ (ignored) and identified by SHA-256 3b96fa3ad318ab9d91db53b25100d5169fafe3a1ecb993e7c36ffff55bf9d8bc; data/translations/en-pickthall-1930.json is derived from it by scripts/import/import-pickthall.js, which only joins wrapped lines. The e-text's own header and licence notice are not part of the shipped data. 8 ayahs (17:32-33, 39:45-46, 45:31-32, 56:25-26) are excluded because the e-text merges each pair under one verse number; they are listed in the alignment report, not guessed. The e-text was 're-proofed against paper copies' by a volunteer from a file of unknown origin, so typographical errors are possible.

gate.commercial_use: yes: the work is in the public domain
gate.attribution: none required by law; credited anyway (NOTICE and the app footer)
gate.modification: permitted (QURRA joins wrapped lines only; text is otherwise verbatim)
gate.third_party_material: the e-text bundles two other translations (not used); a volunteer's re-proofing of the transcription
gate.upstream: print edition (1930) -> volunteer transcription (2005) -> this import
gate.reason: Public-domain work; transcription catalogued as public domain in the USA. Archaic English ('Thou/Thee'), so it is labelled as a 1930 translation.

sources.name: QuranEnc English editions (Rowwad Translation Center; Saheeh; Hilali and Khan)
sources.licence: Republishing permitted verbatim under seven stated conditions (no modification, credit publisher and source, state the version, keep the transcript information, notify the source of notes, keep the translation up to date, no inappropriate advertising).
sources.allowed_use: None until the conditions are resolved.
sources.notes: The terms do not say whether commercial use is allowed, and condition 6 (follow the latest version) is a continuing obligation that a static bundle cannot meet automatically. The Hilali-Khan and Saheeh editions are third-party works. Not imported.

gate.third_party_material: yes for Saheeh and Hilali-Khan
gate.reason: A modern readable English option, but commercial use and the update obligation need a written answer.
